newsitem.title: INDIA: India cuts import duties on software, electronics.
newsitem.headline: India cuts import duties on software, electronics.

text.p: The Indian government on Friday proposed abolishing the import duty on computer software and slashing import tariffs on computer and electronic parts.
Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced the proposed cuts in presenting the budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year starting on April. The cuts would have to be approved by parliament.

He said the government planned to cut the duty on integrated circuits, colour monitor tubes, cartridge tape drives, digital video disc drives and computer parts other than populated printed circuit boards (PCBs), to 10 percent from 20 percent.
The government proposed cutting the import duty on populated PCBs as well as components used in telecommunication equipment, mobile telephones and radio pagers to 20 percent from 30 percent.
The import duty on colour picture tubes would be slashed to 30 percent from 35 percent, and that on telecommunications equipment to 30 percent from 40 percent, he said.
"The spread of information technology has radicaly altered conventional wisdom on growth strategies," Chidambaram told parliament.
